idiom_name: input-only render component plus a separate supply step (values down, events up)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: decide per subtree which half owns what. The render half takes exactly the values it displays plus a callback for every event it raises, performs no data access and mutates nothing it was given; the supply half obtains the data (fetch, subscribe, query, template context), owns loading, error and empty handling, and renders the view half with values down and events up. Where the platform already has a state-holder idiom - a custom hook, state hoisting, a ViewModel, a signal owner - put the supply half there instead of in a wrapper component: the wrapper is the classic form, and it stays justified when the data source must be injectable per screen (tests, stories, route boundaries) or when several views really share one source. Enforce the direction of the dependency: the view may not import the data source, and the supply half should contain no markup beyond composition.
pitfalls: Letting the render half reach for the data source directly recreates the coupling the split removes, and the reuse it was meant to buy disappears.
Owning the data above where it is read re-renders a wider subtree than necessary; hoist to the lowest common ancestor, not to the screen by default.
The boundary is a convention, not a compiler check: without naming and review discipline the codebase drifts into containers that stay thin and children that quietly fetch.

Wrong move: Import a store or API client in the presentational view -> the view is no longer source-agnostic and literal stories need provider or network setup -> instead pass data and callbacks through the props contract.

Wrong move: Add a container around every leaf -> wrapper and prop-forwarding sprawl obscure ownership and add render overhead -> instead introduce a supply half only at a real reuse, route, or data-boundary seam.

Wrong move: Keep a hook or store and a container as parallel owners -> updates diverge and loading or error state becomes contradictory -> instead choose one owner and let the other layer only adapt its contract.
